### Author Background and Reception
Ama Owusu, a debut novelist, was born in Kumasi, Ghana, in 1990. She studied English and Linguistics at the University of Ghana, earning her BA in 2012, and then completed an MFA in Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia in 2015. Her short fiction has been published in well-known literary outlets such as Granta and Jalada Africa. Her debut novel, **Glassy-eyed** (2023), published by Cassava Press, has received a positive reception and was longlisted for the Etisalat Prize for Literature. The novel is noted for exploring multigenerational themes within the Boateng-Asante family in Accra.

For more details, you can visit her [author profile on Cassava Press](https://openbooks.net/authors/ama-owusu) or read an [interview with Brittle Paper](https://openbooks.net/interviews/ama-owusu) where she discusses her creative process and the inspirations behind her work.

### Critical Reception and Conversation
**Glassy-eyed** has been well-received, being featured in reviews from notable publications. It earned four stars from The Africa Report and is listed as an Editor's Choice in Brittle Paper. Additionally, it has received a recommended status from Chimurenga and has been shortlisted for the Commonwealth Writers Prize in the Africa region for 2024. Its first printing sold out within six weeks, indicating strong initial demand and interest. Further insights into the critical landscape can be found in the [Critical Round-Up](https://openbooks.net/reviews/glassy-eyed).

### Digital Availability
The novel has the ISBN 978-1-73625-441-8. Unfortunately, the digital version appears to be restricted to institutional subscriptions, limiting individual access to the full text. So far, I have retrieved a preview of Chapter 1 only.

### Excerpt from the First Chapter
Here is an excerpt from Chapter 1 of **Glassy-eyed**:

> "The workshop smelled of sand and heat and something else — something mineral, a smell that had no common name but that Nana had associated, since childhood, with the moment before things changed form. Her grandfather called it the smell of possibility, which she had always found romantic to the point of embarrassment. After twenty years, she simply called it home.
>
> She arrived in the early morning, before anyone else, the way she always arrived on days she needed to think. The furnace had been banked overnight and the glass pots still held the remnants of yesterday's work — a green that her grandfather had mixed in the 1970s from a formula written in a notebook..."

This excerpt provides insight into the novel's thematic foundation and character focus.

### Next Steps
1. You can attempt to access the full text through institutional resources or library services using the ISBN.
2. Consider checking online retailers or libraries for purchasing or borrowing options if you are under a tight deadline.
3. For deeper analysis, you may want to explore the critical reviews that discuss its themes and character development further.
